Subject: Private deployment security discovery & evidence checklist

Oliver — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on follow-ups for Medican Health's private deployment evaluation.

Summary of what we heard
- Goal: run Redwood in a private/VPC or on-prem arrangement with strict network isolation and HIPAA controls for PHI processing.
- High-level asks: SOC 2 Type II report, encryption at rest/in transit details, KMS/HSM integration, network diagram, and vendor questionnaire for procurement.

Immediate next steps (what Redwood will do)
1) Share current SOC 2 Type II (most recent) and our SOC roadmap (we’ll attach the PDF).
2) Provide a lightweight network-diagram template you can populate (attached drawio).
3) Start the vendor security questionnaire — Monica will own completing the technical sections and will reach out for any specific artifact requests.
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive to walk your infra/security team through our Private deployment options (VPC peering, private control plane, air-gapped on-prem patterns).

Questions for you
- Do you need a fully air-gapped option or is a VPC/private control plane sufficient for the initial pilot?
- Who from your security/procurement teams should we send the questionnaire link to (we’ve CC’d procurement in this thread for visibility)?
- Any hard deadlines for evidence delivery or an upcoming audit window we should be aware of?

Attachments: call-notes-20260427.txt (brief meeting notes)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the documents and Monica will coordinate the questionnaire items.

—
Maya Srinivasan

Thanks Maya — useful recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we dive in: 

1) SOC 2: we need the most recent Type II with the control matrix and any remediations called out. If the report is redacted that’s fine, but please include an artifact showing the scope (systems + shielding for customer data).

2) HIPAA/GDPR: confirm whether Redwood handles any PHI in hosted mode and what the responsibilities split looks like in a private deployment. We’ll want a short responsibilities table for our legal/compliance review.

3) On-prem vs VPC: for the pilot we prefer a VPC/private control plane but we might need an air-gapped on-prem option later. Please indicate which artifacts differ between those modes (e.g., evidence for physical access controls, on-site HSM requirements).

4) Questionnaire: please send a URL or a downloadable form. Procurement wants us to track completion in our vendor portal.

Can you also share the proposed timeline for when Monica will have the initial questionnaire draft? We’re targeting an internal compliance review week of May 17.

Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of IT Security, Medican Health
oliver.grant@medicanhealth.com

Date: Wed, 29 Apr 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment security discovery & evidence checklist

Oliver — appreciate the clarity. Quick answers inline and what we’ll attach now: 

- SOC 2: attaching SOC2_Type2_2025.pdf (redacted report) and a one-page control-scope summary. If you need an unredacted bridge letter, we can arrange that under an NDA.
- HIPAA/GDPR responsibilities: short table below — we’ll formalize into the questionnaire.

  * Redwood (Private/VPC): processes customer workload in your VPC; customer controls network egress and access. Redwood provides the runtime and optional private control plane; we can integrate with your KMS (bring-your-own-key).
  * Customer (Medican): responsible for EHR/PACS ingestion pipelines, internal access controls, and any local audit logging retained on your side for PHI.

- Differences for on-prem air-gap: physical access controls, chain-of-custody for hardware, and on-site HSM requirements are additional artifacts you’ll need; we’ve included an attachment called network-diagram-template.drawio that outlines the difference in control boundaries.

Questionnaire timeline: Monica will circulate the initial draft by EOD Fri, May 7, and will request artifacts in batches. That should give you time to slot the compliance review the week of May 17. If you need things faster we can prioritize key artifacts first (SOC, encryption certs, KMS integration notes).

Attachments included now: SOC2_Type2_2025.pdf, network-diagram-template.drawio

—

Hi Oliver — I’ll own the vendor questionnaire and the evidence collection. Thanks for the timeline note — targeting initial draft to you by May 7 as Ben mentioned.

- May 7: initial draft returned to Medican for review (sections: architecture, encryption, access controls, incident response).
- May 10–14: collect artifacts (SOC, encryption certs, KMS integration docs, network diagrams).
- Week of May 17: technical deep-dive — please share 2x 60-minute slots that work for your infra/security team and we’ll send calendar invites.

Suggested slots for the deep-dive (PST):
- Tue May 18, 11:00–12:00 or Wed May 19, 14:00–15:00
